notes:
Four false statements found by auditing postgresql.org and checking every claim against the live site.

**"Nearly every outbound link is nofollow" counted internal links.** The share divided every nofollowed anchor on every page — internal ones included, repeats counted twice — by the number of external destinations, which is counted once per page with the site's own hosts removed. Two different populations, so the "share" could exceed 100%: PostgreSQL's came out at 956%. Its documentation nofollows the version switcher that offers the same article in fifteen older releases, which is exactly the right thing to do with fifteen near-duplicates, and Docket told it to strip that. Re-measured over seven crawled sites, the two the ratio was wrong about both stop firing — PostgreSQL at 4% and WPBeginner, whose ordinary 56% affiliate policy was being reported as "nearly every", at 56%.

**A mascot and a section were reported as two company names.** PostgreSQL's logo is named "PostgreSQL Elephant Logo", its documentation declares og:site_name "PostgreSQL Documentation", and its homepage declares plain "PostgreSQL". The check drops a spelling contained in another — "Acme" inside "Acme Roofing" is one brand written short and long — but it did that pairwise in order of how often each was seen, so the short canonical name arrived last and was absorbed into whichever longer one it met first. Each spelling now folds onto the shortest one it contains, so the name a site actually declares is the one that survives.

**A tag-manager deployment counted as zero tools per page.** The inventory reads the served HTML merged with the rendered DOM, because a tag manager injects its tags at runtime. The number printed beside that inventory read the served HTML alone, so PostgreSQL's report listed three tools and "max_per_page: 0" in the same breath. The gate that escalates the finding for script bloat read the same zero, which meant it could never fire for the sites it was written for.

**A typeface was named by its CSS escape.** A font family written without quotes escapes its spaces with a backslash, and the report printed one as `font awesome\ 5 free` — a string that is not what the font is called.

Verified true on the same audit, with controls: no caching headers on any page, no compression, three broken outbound links to a Google Summer of Code site that closed years ago, 44 of 45 pages with no meta description, and two pages both titled "PostgreSQL: Donate".
